name: Greenwashing and disclosure claims
blurb: Allegations of misleading disclosure on data centre carbon footprint or power usage effectiveness.
summary: Allegations of misleading disclosure on data centre carbon footprint or power usage effectiveness.

part_3_high_value_red_flags: A broad pollution exclusion that could be interpreted to exclude claims arising from carbon emissions or energy usage disclosures.
A fraud or dishonesty exclusion that applies at the allegation stage rather than only after a final non appealable adjudication.
A prior acts exclusion that bars coverage for misleading statements made before the policy inception date.
A pending or prior litigation exclusion that excludes any claim related to a regulatory inquiry or shareholder demand known before inception.
An insured versus insured exclusion that would bar derivative suits brought by shareholders against directors.
A definition of claim that excludes formal regulatory investigations or pre claim subpoenas, leaving defence costs uncovered.
An ESG specific exclusion or sublimit that caps or removes coverage for greenwashing allegations.
manuscript_wording_and_carve_backs: Negotiate removal of any ESG or sustainability specific exclusion so that unintentional greenwashing claims remain covered.
Amend the fraud and dishonesty exclusion to apply only after a final adjudication establishing deliberate misconduct, not at the pleading stage.
Add a definition of wrongful act that expressly includes negligent misstatement in carbon footprint or PUE disclosures.
Include regulatory investigation costs and pre claim inquiry costs as covered loss within the policy definition.
Provide prior acts coverage for legacy disclosures made before the current policy period, subject to a retroactive date if necessary.
Carve back the pollution exclusion to clarify it does not apply to financial loss claims arising from carbon accounting or energy efficiency statements.
Add a discovery period or extended reporting period of at least 12 months to capture claims made after policy expiry.

part_4_program_structure_and_limits.bi_waiting_period: Not applicable, D&O claims do not have a business interruption waiting period because they cover defence costs and damages, not lost income.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.business_interruption: Not applicable, D&O policies do not provide business interruption cover for greenwashing claims.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.property_eb_equipment: Not applicable, no property or equipment breakdown coverage is relevant to greenwashing and disclosure claims.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.per_occurrence_primary_excess_layered_pr: Not applicable to this D&O exposure, the program uses primary and excess D&O layers with per claim limits rather than per occurrence property limits.

part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.cgl_primary: Not applicable to this D&O exposure, the primary layer is a directors and officers liability policy with Side A, Side B and Side C coverage.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.paper_basis: Claims-made, because greenwashing and disclosure claims arise from wrongful acts that may span multiple policy periods and are reported when a demand, suit or regulatory investigation is first made against the insured.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.excess_umbrella_towers: Excess D&O layers sit above the primary policy, typically following form, with drop down provisions if underlying limits are exhausted by payment of loss.

part_1_core_third_party_liability_exposu: Securities class actions by shareholders alleging that inflated ESG credentials caused artificial share price inflation and subsequent loss.
Regulatory investigations by the SEC, FCA or ASIC into misleading sustainability disclosures under anti fraud or consumer protection rules.
Derivative suits by shareholders against directors for breach of fiduciary duty in approving inaccurate carbon footprint statements.
Consumer or competitor claims under unfair competition or false advertising laws where data centre customers relied on PUE figures.
Contractual disputes with hyperscale tenants or colocation customers who negotiated service level agreements based on disclosed PUE.
Claims by lenders or green bond investors who provided financing conditioned on achieving certain carbon intensity metrics.
Reputational harm claims from business partners or industry groups alleging greenwashing damaged their own ESG standing.

underwriter_wants_to_know: How the data centre calculates and discloses power usage effectiveness and whether the methodology has changed over time.
Whether any third party auditor or independent engineer has verified the carbon footprint and PUE figures in public filings or marketing materials.
The identity of any regulators or stock exchanges that have already made inquiries about the company's sustainability disclosures.
The extent to which investors, lenders or customers relied on the carbon footprint or PUE statements when making decisions.
Whether the company has made forward looking statements about future carbon neutrality or PUE targets that could be alleged as misleading.
The company's history of restating ESG metrics or correcting prior disclosures.
The directors and officers involved in approving the disclosures and any personal trading around those announcements.
